title: Count Distinct Numbers on Board
summary: Given a positive integer n, place it on a board.
statement: Given a positive integer n, place it on a board. Each day, for 10^9 days, for every number x on the board, find all numbers 1 <= i <= n where x % i equals 1, and place these numbers on the board. Return the count of distinct numbers on the board after 10^9 days. Once a number is placed, it remains on the board. The modulo operation (x % i) is used to determine which numbers to place.
constraints: Initially only n is on the board.
Repeatedly, for every board value x, add every positive i with x%i=1.
Return the number of distinct values after 10^9 days, when the process is stable.
reference_solution:
def count_distinct_board_numbers(n):
    return 1 if n==1 else n-1
hints: For each x greater than two, x%(x-1)=1, so the process repeatedly adds x-1 down to two.
The stabilized count is therefore n-1.
Closure supplies exactly values two through n, while one can never be added because every value modulo one is zero.
editorial: Closure supplies exactly values two through n, while one can never be added because every value modulo one is zero.

tests.explanation: Values four, three, and two are eventually added beside the original five, giving four distinct values.
No new positive value satisfies one modulo i equals one, so only one remains.
